title: Smart Locks vs. Motion Sensors: What Self Storage Operators Really Get
summary: Discover why smart locks like Nokē outperform motion sensors in self storage, enhancing security, automating processes, and driving revenue for operators.
body_markdown:
Motion sensors are showing up at more self storage facilities, but few owner operators actually know what they're getting with in-unit motion sensors. The pitch for motion sensors is simple. The devices cost the operator very little to add, they install quickly, and the management company earns a revenue share.


But a low upfront cost isn't the same as low cost. Before you add another device to your units, it's worth asking what it actually does for your facility, your tenants, and your bottom line.


## The case for motion sensors


To be fair, motion-sensor-only devices have one real advantage: they're a light lift to install. There's no lock to replace and little disruption to your site.


That's where the advantages end.


## Where motion sensors alone fall short


**The batteries are locked inside the unit.** Once a unit is rented, you can't reach the device to replace its batteries. When it dies, it stays dead until move-out.


**Tenants can bring their own.** A consumer motion sensor is cheap and easy to buy. A device tenants can replicate on their own gives them little reason to pay a premium for yours.


**They don't automate rentals.** A sensor can't let a new tenant into their unit, so your rental process stays exactly as manual as it is today.


**They don't improve security.** A sensor may report that something moved. It doesn't keep anyone out, and it doesn't deter anyone from trying.


**They don't provide actionable data.** Movement alerts aren't the same as knowing who accessed a unit, when, and whether the door is secured.


**They don't automate overlocking or delinquency.** Your team still walks the property, cuts locks, and applies overlocks by hand.


In short, a motion sensor adds a device to your units without changing how your facility runs.


## What a smart security system does differently


Nokē is a complete smart entry system, purpose-built for self storage, from the gate to the unit door. Instead of watching just for motion, it controls and records every entry, and that changes how your facility operates.


**It secures every unit, vacant or occupied.** Nokē protects units whether they're rented or not, and tells you each door's status in real time.


**It improves security.** Facilities using Nokē see 95%+ fewer claims. Operators are already moving this direction: in Modern Storage Media's[2025 security survey](https://www.modernstoragemedia.com/msm-exclusives/crime-crackdown-msm-survey-reveals-fewer-incidents-more-security) , smart locks posted the largest year-over-year adoption gain of any security measure, and 89% of operators said crime hurts the industry's public image. A visible smart lock on every door is also a deterrent before anyone tries anything.


**It adds security-grade sensors where you want them.** Many Nokē models offer optional security-grade sensors. You get the monitoring a motion sensor promises, plus a lock that actually secures the unit.


**It automates rentals.** With automated onboarding, tenants can rent online and access their unit without waiting on your staff.


**It automates overlocking and delinquency.** Overlocks and unlocks happen automatically based on payment status. No lock cutting and no site walks.


**It delivers actionable data and insights.** Shared keys let you see every user tied to a unit and how each unit is used, so you get a clear picture of activity across your property.


## The revenue question


Motion sensors are often sold on revenue share. Nokē drives revenue directly. Operators use Nokē to charge premium rates and technology fees, because tenants can see and feel the difference in security and convenience every time they visit.


Add labor savings from automated rentals and delinquency, plus insurance savings from fewer claims, and the return grows well beyond a revenue split.
